question: A QoS policy on Cisco UCS must meet these requirements: no-drop class must be configured; and jumbo frames must be enabled without fragmentation. Which configuration must be implemented to meet these conditions?
options: Configure slow-drain timers and specify an MTU value of 9100 bytes.
Create a Flow Control Policy and specify an MTU value of 9000 bytes.
Create a QoS system class and specify an MTU value of 9216 bytes.
Configure Platinum system class and specify an MTU value of 9100 bytes.
theory: A no-drop (lossless) traffic class combined with jumbo frames that must not fragment points to configuring the Ethernet QoS System Class settings directly: enabling a no-drop class configures buffer/pause behavior for lossless delivery, and setting the class's MTU to 9216 bytes — the maximum jumbo MTU Cisco UCS QoS system classes support — ensures frames of up to that size pass through without needing fragmentation. Flow control policies and slow-drain timers address different problems (pause frame handling and congestion detection), and Platinum's own default MTU (9000) doesn't match the 9216 ceiling the QoS system class itself supports. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Network Management, QoS System Classes and Jumbo MTU)
